routed.text: Carried from Q-014 (from S04), which matched S10 by its node and was closed there as explained, unaddressed, because a spec touch may not write the Phase Plan (DEC-095). Original text: ADR-002 for the web app's plan: one module of pure functions taking the zone as an argument (instant to wall time, a date to [start of date, start of next date), the form's quarter-hour instants, the repeated-hour and other-date marks), tested in isolation on 2027-03-28 (23 hours, 92 slots, no 01:xx) and 2027-10-31 (25 hours, 100 slots, 01:00 to 01:45 twice as BST then GMT) per hsdd/auto/experiments/time-model-intl/; Node.js 24 has no global Temporal, so use Intl or a library on it, or a polyfill; en-GB gives 'Thu 5 Nov', HH:mm with hourCycle h23, GMT and BST (en-US gives GMT+1); Vitest runs with TZ set to a third zone; the browser's clock only picks the Rooms screen's opening date; the overlap message is built from the refusal's instants, not from error.message.

Carried from Q-019 (from S05), which matched S10 by its node and was closed there as explained, unaddressed, because a spec touch may not write the Phase Plan (DEC-095). Original text: booking-api@v1 for the web's plan: web/src/test/fetchStub.ts matches String(input) against request.path, but the rooms fixtures' paths carry unencoded colons (/api/rooms?from=2026-11-05T00:00:00.000Z&to=...) while URLSearchParams writes %3A, so compare decoded URLs or build the query without encoding (the producer accepts both). A 204 fixture's body is null and new Response(body, { status: 204 }) throws on any body, so the stub answers it with no body. Fixtures carry clock and given, which explain the answer and are never sent. AC-5.3's message is written from error.conflict's roomName, start and end in the user's zone (G18); the codes to branch on are UNAUTHORIZED, VALIDATION_FAILED, BOOKING_TOO_LONG, BOOKING_STARTED, BOOKING_TOO_FAR_AHEAD, BOOKING_CONFLICT, BOOKING_NOT_FOUND (a second tab already cancelled) and BOOKING_NOT_YOURS. The form may offer end times up to start + 8 hours and dates up to 365 days ahead, but the backend's answer decides. Lists arrive sorted; no client sort is needed. consumers names simple-login.web.5 provisionally (DEC-053).

Carried from Q-023 (from S07), which matched S10 by its node and was closed there as explained, unaddressed, because a spec touch may not write the Phase Plan (DEC-095). Original text: profile-api@v2 G4 promises timeZone in every 200 profile; G5 says the web takes the user's zone from it only, never the browser's, and shows no time rather than guess one when a profile lacks it (a backend that predates the field; backend and web ship separately, PRD v2 Team and delivery). Read from the code, not run: decideProfile ignores unknown fields, so the shipped web reads the new fixtures unchanged. The appended plan adds timeZone to the web's own Profile type and to Home (AC-2.1, AC-2.5) and decides absence: today a missing field makes the whole profile 'unavailable', which would also hide Home's other rows.

From S10's touch (DEC-092, DEC-093). The Overview no longer states how the app moves between screens; D4 ('No router (RFC §6): the screen is a function of the session value') and D5 are now its only statement, and the D4 revisit (DEC-012) has three screens to cover: Home to Rooms and back (PRD v2 Screens: Book a room, Home), which screen shows after sign-in and on reload, and what Rooms does on a 401 or an unreachable backend. D1 notices expiry only when GET /api/me answers 401 on load; booking-api@v1 G16 answers 401 UNAUTHORIZED at every endpoint, so a booking request from Rooms or a Cancel on Home can be the first to see an expired token (PRD v2 AC-2.3). The header's Isolation strategy now says the time functions are tested on their own on London's clock-change days and every test runs with TZ set to a zone that is neither account's nor UTC (ADR-002); the plan's gate command or Vitest configuration is where that is set. Owns names turning instants into dates and times in the user's zone and back, and their display format, as this node's (ADR-002 Decisions 4 and 7).

S10 restated Purpose, Owns and Isolation strategy (in hsdd/spec/simple-login.web.md and the embedded summary in hsdd/spec/simple-login.md) and the Overview, citing PRD v2 by section (Screens, US-1 to US-6, AC-2.5, AC-4.2 to AC-4.4, AC-5.2, AC-5.3), ADR-002, profile-api@v2 G5 and booking-api@v1 G18 (DEC-089).
